def-measure: Curvature or radius from data the Earth's radius never entered: times, local angles, lengths measured on the ground, measured heights, latitudes and longitudes taken as angles.
def-check: Real data set against the globe, or data that were produced with a globe model at some point, even if that model was taken out again afterwards.
def-model: What a model predicts; no measured data.
legend-p: Each section that shows evidence carries one of three labels. The rule is strict: a distance in kilometres taken from coordinates, a map or a terrain model already contains the Earth's radius, and so do satellite orbits (WGS84), the GRS80 reference gravity, the IGRF magnetic model and any speed that was itself measured with globe distances. Latitudes and longitudes, taken as angles, do not. A measurement that touched the radius once stays a check, even if the radius was removed again later.
legend-measure: the curvature or the radius comes out of data the radius never entered.
legend-check: real data compared with the globe, or produced with a globe model at some point.
legend-model: what a model predicts, nothing measured.
legend-none: Sections without a label explain, tell history, answer objections or give the flat model its best case.
enters-avia-eot: NOAA removed the Eötvös effect with the GRS80 radii; putting it back needs those radii.
enters-avia-gc: route lengths in km computed from the airports' coordinates.
enters-azim-ecl: the published eclipse bearing comes from an ephemeris that places the observer on the ellipsoid.
enters-ct-stars: star altitudes from a planetarium program at positions on the globe.
enters-ct-crest: crest angles from distances in km computed from coordinates and map heights.
enters-curv-map: distances to the tower read on a map.
enters-dip-own: the camera's level is set by summits whose angles need their distances in km.
enters-dip-mlo: the Sun's altitude from an ephemeris, the observatory's horizon from a terrain model; the coast's sunset is computed.
enters-fou-lat: published rates set against sin φ; fine as a test, no radius comes out of it.
enters-gps-eph: satellite orbits broadcast in the WGS84 frame, whose scale was fixed by stations on the ellipsoid.
enters-grav-arc: meridian arcs published after reduction on the spheroid.
enters-grav-richer: compared with a reference gravity formula of the GRS80 family.
enters-grav-mass: the Earth's mass computed with its radius.
enters-hh-map: distances and heights read on maps and terrain models.
enters-mag-igrf: magnetic latitude from the IGRF pole, a model fitted on the globe.
enters-obs-lidar: the ridge's distance from the terrain model, the Sun from an ephemeris.
enters-ref-k: k is derived from the angle s/R, which uses the radius.
enters-rx-eph: satellite orbits broadcast in the WGS84 frame, whose scale was fixed by stations on the ellipsoid.
enters-seis-v: the wave speeds were established with distances measured on the globe.
enters-surv-tri: the spherical excess compared with the globe's prediction.
enters-surv-red: the 1900 triangulation sides were reduced to sea level on the spheroid, and the corrected radius uses k = 0.13, a coefficient measured with the radius known. The 1977 EDM distances are raw slope distances; without k they give the measured section below.
enters-sun-alm: noon altitudes from an almanac computed for positions on the globe.
enters-seis-mesh: what turns the mesh's unit into kilometres is the speed of the law, established with distances measured on the globe; and the readings kept are those the ISC names "P" (compared with a travel-time table built on a spherical Earth), 25–95° from our own relocation, a selection made with a globe fit. The times alone give the shape; this is where the size enters.
enters-seis-label: no radius and no travel-time table in the fits, but the readings used are those the ISC names "P", a name it gives by comparing each arrival with a travel-time table built on a spherical Earth. A label-free check (the first reported arrival at each station) gives the same verdict.
enters-orb-sdo: the apparent radius is computed by the SDO pipeline from the spacecraft–Sun distance, an ephemeris.
enters-orb-dop: the observed velocity is rebuilt by adding back a barycentric correction computed from ephemerides, and the Sun's declination comes from one.
enters-orb-star: the observed velocity is rebuilt by adding back the barycentric correction, computed from ephemerides.
enters-orb-radar: the antenna's place on the Earth, on the ellipsoid, moves each distance by up to 5,800 km, and today's orbits rest in part on the radar ranging of later decades.
enters-orb-psr: the timing model places each telescope by its coordinates on the Earth, and takes the shape of the Earth's orbit from an ephemeris whose scale rests partly on radar ranging.
enters-orb-transit: the baseline between the stations is in Earth radii, so the distance comes out in Earth radii and is turned into kilometres with that radius; the orbits' shape comes from an ephemeris.
enters-moon-llr: the Moon's direction (declination, hour angle) comes from a lunar theory, and the station's geocentric latitude uses the ellipsoid's flattening.
enters-moon-ecl: the distances of the Moon and the Sun in km come from an ephemeris (DE440), and the catalogue kept only the timings whose layer height, computed from the Earth's radius, lies between −50 and +250 km.
enters-ref-air: the globe's rays are traced over a sphere of 6,371 km; the distances to Bordighera and to the targets and horizons of the contributed photographs come from coordinates; the weather models (ERA5, GFS, AROME) are built on a spherical Earth.
enters-ref-igra: k = R/ρ is the ray's curvature divided by the Earth's: the radius is its unit.
enters-grav-tower: the prediction each reading is compared with is built from a normal gravity field that contains the Earth's radius, and the paper publishes only the differences.
enters-hh-bord: the 49 km from the balcony to Bordighera, computed from coordinates on a sphere of radius R.
enters-seis-shadow: the stations' coordinates come from maps, and the phase names (P, Pdif, PKP) are the ISC's, given by comparing each reading with the ak135 travel-time tables built for a spherical Earth.
enters-seis-waves: the kinds of waves and the direction each P wave came from are read off the records alone, with each sensor's orientation; the epicentres the directions are compared with are the ISC's, located with travel-time tables built for a spherical Earth.
enters-cases-p2p: the 15.2 km between the piers is computed from their coordinates on a sphere of radius R.
enters-grav-tides: nowhere: the records are compared with the tide that gravity on a globe and Kepler's laws predict; only the harmonic analysis takes the frequencies of its lines from the Moon's and Sun's motions, and the periods read off the records use the clock alone.
prov-tip: Where these numbers come from: the data files, how each was obtained, and the code that computes them
prov-explain: beside every file, a .explain says where it comes from, how it was obtained, its hash, and why it is not in the repository when it is not.
prov-how-api: answer of a public web API
prov-how-transcription: typed by hand from a printed or scanned source
prov-how-ours: written by us (a list or a choice), not measured
prov-pub-no: Not in the repository, only its hash and source:
prov-norepo: The public repository is being prepared: the paths are relative to it.
prov-redo: To redo it: fog fetch <id>, then fog build <target> (tools/), and compare with the generated file.
